title: Quotes
summary: Build a quote from your product list, send it for approval, and turn the approved one into a job or an invoice.
html:
A quote is a priced proposal to a customer or a lead. Once they approve it, it becomes a job you can work on, or an invoice you can send — you do not retype anything.

Creating one

Quotes → Create Quote, then pick the customer. The quote is built from lines, and each line can be:

  • A product from your product list, which brings its description and price with it. See Products.
  • A free text line you type in, for work that is not a catalogue item.

Each line has a quantity, a unit price and a tax setting. The quote total is the sum, with tax calculated per line rather than on the total, so mixed tax rates on one quote work correctly.

Sending it

Email Quote sends it to the customer's primary contact using a template you can edit under Templates. The email contains a link that lets the customer open the quote without logging in.

Approval

The customer opens the link and either approves or declines. Approving records a drawn signature, the date and their IP address against the quote, so there is a record of who agreed to what.

You can also mark a quote approved yourself, for the case where the customer agreed on the phone.

Turning an approved quote into work

An approved quote has a Create Invoice button. If you track the work first, create a job from it instead and invoice at the end — see Jobs.

Converting copies the lines across. Editing the invoice afterwards does not change the quote, so the quote stays as a record of what was agreed.

Quote numbers

Two settings control numbering:

  • quote_name_incrementing — switch automatic numbering on.
  • quote_name_incrementing_next — the next number to be used.

Set the second one before you start if you are continuing a sequence from another system.
